Synopsis:
If Balthazar is alive when the player reaches Nightsong, they will encounter a dialogue where Balthazar and Nightsong square off. The player has one last chance to betray Balthazar and prevent him from taking Nightsong to Moonrise.

Cluster Contexts:
- SHA_NightsongPrison_NecroAndNightsong.json: Balthazar is alive and confronts Nightsong (Aylin) while she is held in a narrow, magically bound cage; warding "magi-hands" keep her from escaping. Nightsong is defiant and bitter, invoking Ketheric—whose immortality she apparently helps sustain—and spitting contempt at her captor. Balthazar speaks patronizingly, claims to have "gifted" her and says he intends to take her back to General Thorm / Moonrise, noting he has taken precautions to secure her. Shadowheart objects fiercely, and the player (referred to as a would‑be Justiciar) is present and given one last chance to betray Balthazar and prevent him from carrying Nightsong away.
- COL_Necromancer_EnterRoom.json: A player walked into Balthazar's chambers in the colony, while Balthazar is alive, and was spotted by him (or one of his undead). Balthazar reacts with hostility, but players can convince him that they have been turned into thralls.This can only happen if Balthazar is alive at this point and you didn't try the Audience with the Absolute. If you did not send Nightsong to Ketheric, Balthazar would have died in combat in her prison.This dialog will also play when interacting with Balthazar in this route.
- SHA_Necromancer_Chosen.json: The player meets Balthazar, the necromancer, in his temporary command centre in the Shar temple. They find him at an altar, repairing one of his damaged undead, while other minions bustle around. Balthazar has been sent by Ketheric Thorm to recover Nightsong, but has been unable to clear a path to her vault. He decides to recruit the player, upon recognising them as tadpoled. The player can agree or decline, and can possibly persuade him to loan his flesh golem to aid their exploration.
- SHA_NightsongPrison_NightsongsFate.json: The player encounter Nightsong, an angelic Aasimar and daughter of Selune who has been trapped in the Shadowfell for a century, first to serve as fodder for Dark Justiciars to kill (they must kill a Selunite to ascend), and then to provide Ketheric with immortality through a soul cage. The player can meet her either alone or with Balthazar. Nightsong is defiant and full of rage. She is immortal, so her current trials are, for her, an annoyance, an indignity, but she knows she will ultimately have her revenge. She regards the player with haughty defiance until she is convinced the player is on her side. If she's freed, she'll have 2 big cinematics of becoming free and cleansed by Selune.
- MOO_Executioner.json: Dialogue with Z'rell when she's upstairs. This takes place after the execution scene, and involves Z'rell mind-melding to see how players dealt with the goblins, and testing their 'desire' to be one with the Absolute via a second mind-meld. She then gives them the mission to aid Balthazar, giving them the key to his chamber, and instructing them to find evidence of where he can be found.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Nightsong: Balthazar. Come to add more bars to my cage. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: She paces the narrow cage where she's kept, like a tiger. She looks down as she paces, not yet deigning to make eye contact. (node 65)
- Nightsong: Or perhaps to lead this would-be Justiciar's blade directly to my heart? || [context] CinematicNodeContext:  On "this Justiciar"," abruptly turns to the player and points an accusing finger. As she moves forward out of position, magical hands grab around her wrists arms and shoulers, holding her back. She looks down at them and grimaces in rage, then steps back into place. This is how she's bound: If she moves too far, she'll be pulled back by the magi-hands. (node 38)
- Nightsong: I invite you: heap more sins upon your head. My retribution will be all the sweeter for them. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Stock still. Cold. Staring Balthazar dead in the eyes.NodeContext: With a deep, seething foreboding (node 32)
- Balthazar: All this time, and you still fail to appreciate the gifts I bestowed on you, Aylin. Sad, to see a thing of beauty not recognise its own worth. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Displeased poutNodeContext: A little displeased and admonishing (node 51)
- Balthazar: But General Thorm - he appreciates you. And he wants you close at hand, so I am here to whisk you back to him. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Brightening upNodeContext: Tone brightening up a little (node 56)
- Nightsong: Ketheric. I welcome the sight of him, after these hundred years. He whose immortality I supply with my very soul. || [context] NodeContext: She spits on the floor of her cage after 'Ketheric' (node 48)
- Balthazar: General. Thorm. I'm sure you'll be on your best behaviour for him. But just in case, I've taken some precautions. || [context] NodeContext: Chastising. (node 61)
- Balthazar: Keep back. It will take quite some concentration to secure Aylin for her little journey. (node 50)
- Shadowheart: The Nightsong is Shar's sacrifice - she's my destiny. He cannot have her! || [context] NodeContext: Urgent. Her sacred mission is in jeopardy (node 62)

The player meets Balthazar, the necromancer, in his temporary command centre in the Shar temple. They find him at an altar, repairing one of his damaged undead, while other minions bustle around. Balthazar has been sent by Ketheric Thorm to recover Nightsong, but has been unable to clear a path to her vault. He decides to recruit the player, upon recognising them as tadpoled. The player can agree or decline, and can possibly persuade him to loan his flesh golem to aid their exploration.

The player encounter Nightsong, an angelic Aasimar and daughter of Selune who has been trapped in the Shadowfell for a century, first to serve as fodder for Dark Justiciars to kill (they must kill a Selunite to ascend), and then to provide Ketheric with immortality through a soul cage. The player can meet her either alone or with Balthazar. Nightsong is defiant and full of rage. She is immortal, so her current trials are, for her, an annoyance, an indignity, but she knows she will ultimately have her revenge. She regards the player with haughty defiance until she is convinced the player is on her side. If she's freed, she'll have 2 big cinematics of becoming free and cleansed by Selune.

context: Balthazar is alive and the scene takes place at Nightsong’s prison in the Shar temple: Aylin (Nightsong) is confined in a narrow, magically warded cage where magi‑hands hold her if she tries to move, and the player (the would‑be Justiciar) and Shadowheart are present. Nightsong is bitter and defiant, spitting contempt at Balthazar and openly invoking Ketheric—whose immortality she apparently helps sustain. Balthazar, acting as a necromantic agent of Ketheric/General Thorm, speaks patronizingly, insists he has “gifted” her and intends to take her back to Moonrise, noting he’s taken precautions to secure her. The player is given one last chance in this confrontation to betray Balthazar and stop him from carrying Nightsong away.
